script: My boss accused me of AI, but I blamed him—shocking fallout!. I was handed a deck for the board meeting. The boss said, "We need a clean comparison of last year's numbers to this year's." I am new, so I grabbed the 2025 Annual Report and copied the stats. I barely tweaked the wording so the numbers lined up. I thought, "No buzz‑words, keep it straightforward." (Honestly, it was fine.) Then the boss pulls me aside. He's not happy. He says, "You can use AI to edit, but it has to be your own work." The slide sounds like it was written by a bot, and it's not even tailored to the program. I remembered when I first joined. He handed me the Annual Report he'd written and whispered, "I didn't have time, so I used ChatGPT a lot." So I go, "I pulled that straight from the Annual Report. If it sounds AI‑generated, that's because you used AI to write it." He wasn't amused. Am I the jerk? (I know, right?) The audacity is real. I am better at pulling data than blaming the boss for his own shortcuts. The stakes? I risk losing trust, but I am keeping my integrity. The tension? I am stuck between pointing out his past shortcuts and facing his wrath. The resolution? I stood my ground and left the office, knowing the truth was on my side.
